Instructor(s)

Principal Joseph Wang

Joseph is the CIO of Monetary Macro LLC, author of Central Banking 101, and operator of Fedguy.com. Earlier in his career he was a senior trader on the Federal Reserve's Open Markets Desk, a credit analyst at S&P Ratings, and an attorney in New York. Through his career he has had the opportunity to study the financial system from the outside as a market participant, but also from its very center on the Desk. His work aims shed light on what often appears to be an opaque system, and to bridge the gap between academia and practice when it comes to financial markets.
Joseph holds a B.A. in Economics from Northwestern University, a J.D. from Columbia Law School, and an MSc. in Financial Economics from Oxford University.

Joseph Wang

Joseph Wang

Central Banking contributing editor Joseph Wang is a former senior trader on the US Federal Reserve’s Open Market Trading Desk, where he implemented monetary policy and studied the mechanics of the US dollar financial system. He is the author of Central banking 101 , and proprietor of Fed Guy , an educational site for those interested in financial plumbing. He holds degrees in both law and finance, and has over a decade of experience spanning regulation, capital markets and monetary policy.

Former Federal Reserve trader Joseph Wang provides an accessible introduction to modern central banking systems, monetary policy implementation, and financial market operations. The book explains how central banks influence liquidity, interest rates, inflation, and banking stability through tools such as open market operations, reserve management, and balance sheet policy. Combining macroeconomic theory with practical insights from financial markets, Wang examines the relationship between central banks, commercial banks, government debt markets, and the broader global economy
